title: fix(protocol): declare model API-key editing contracts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated clients cannot describe requests or successful responses for the existing `models.authSetApiKey` method.

## User Impact

Clients gain typed key-editing requests and results, including saved-with-refresh-warning responses. Malformed fields receive standard request-validation errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical protocol schemas replace the handler's duplicate shape checks. Key persistence keeps its existing writer. The necessary schema and public exports add 23 lines; the typed handler adds seven. Regenerated workboard asset references account for its bundled protocol registry.

## Evidence

The baseline generator omitted both definitions. The 151-case integration and compiled TypeScript/Swift consumers pass for the unchanged protocol patch. The final head also passes type, lint, protocol, and generated-asset checks. Exact tested source identities are retained with the proof.

Hosted CI fails only on the stale Docker fixture name introduced in #148074. The exact test fails identically on the CI base and merge; this PR changes none of its inputs. All other required checks passed.

## Compatibility

Unknown request fields, empty agent selection, administrator scope, semantic key checks and refresh warnings remain supported. No method, protocol version or storage change. The stable release predates this method.

## Consumers

Existing Models requests remain valid; generated Swift types now describe their wire fields.

## Invalidation

Credential save still precedes the existing auth refresh.

## Tests

Public validation, real persistence, invalid-input nonmutation, administrator access and saved-warning results.

Refs #144420.
